question: Your customer support agent's MCP tools now have detailed descriptions that state when to use lookup_order to check an order's status and when to use process_refund to issue an approved refund. Before the next release, you review the system prompt for wording that could override these well-written descriptions. Which system prompt instruction is the most likely to cause unintended tool selection?

options.text: Keep replies short and friendly, and summarize the agreed resolution at the end of each conversation.
options.reason: This instruction controls tone and format only. It creates no association between a word in the request and a tool, so it cannot misroute tool selection.

options.text: Escalate to a human agent when the customer explicitly asks for one or when policy does not cover the request.
options.reason: These are condition-based escalation criteria that the guide endorses. They do not tie a single word to a tool, so they do not override the tool descriptions.

options.text: Confirm the customer's identity with get_customer before you discuss any order or account details.
options.reason: This instruction sets a step order that agrees with the purpose of get_customer. It is not a keyword trigger that conflicts with the lookup_order or process_refund descriptions.

options.text: Whenever a customer message contains the word refund, call process_refund right away to resolve the request.
options.reason: This keyword-sensitive instruction ties the word refund to process_refund. It overrides the descriptions, so refund-status questions that need lookup_order go to the wrong tool.
